title: Syphilis Infection During Pregnancy: Risks and Health Impacts
excerpt: Syphilis infection during pregnancy can cause serious health risks and complications for both mother and baby.
content:
## Overview of Syphilis Infection During Pregnancy
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum. When a pregnant woman contracts syphilis, the disease can be transmitted to the fetus, causing serious health risks and complications.

## Risks and Health Impacts
Syphilis infection during pregnancy can cause the following risks:
- Miscarriage: Syphilis can cause miscarriage, especially during the first trimester.
- Stillbirth: Syphilis can also cause stillbirth, when the fetus does not develop or dies in the womb.
- Fetal disease: Syphilis can cause serious diseases in the fetus, including heart disease, lung disease, and neurological disorders.
- Infant mortality: Syphilis can also cause infant mortality, especially during the first few weeks after birth.

## Prevention and Treatment
To prevent syphilis infection during pregnancy, pregnant women should:
- Get tested for syphilis during pregnancy
- Use condoms during sex
- Avoid sex with people who have a high risk of syphilis infection
If syphilis is detected, pregnant women should receive treatment immediately with antibiotics. Early treatment can help minimize the risks and health impacts for both mother and baby.

## Nutrition and Diet
Pregnant women with syphilis should pay attention to their diet and nutrition to help their body fight the disease. Some nutritious foods that can help support health include:
- Fruits and vegetables rich in vitamins and minerals
- Meat and fish rich in protein and iron
- Dairy products rich in calcium and vitamin D
Pregnant women should also avoid foods that can harm their health, including:
- Undercooked or raw foods
- Foods containing preservatives or additives
To have a healthy diet, pregnant women can refer to our [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner) or [prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) category on our website.

## When to Seek Help
Pregnant women should seek help immediately if they experience any of the following symptoms:
- Abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding
- Fever or chills
- Headache or body aches
Pregnant women should also consult their doctor if they have any questions or concerns about syphilis or their health during pregnancy.

For more information on syphilis infection during pregnancy, pregnant women can refer to the following sources:
- World Health Organization (WHO)
- Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
- Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC)

## Conclusion
Syphilis infection during pregnancy is a serious health issue that can cause risks and complications for both mother and baby. Pregnant women should pay attention to their diet and nutrition, get tested for syphilis, and receive treatment immediately if detected. faqs.question: What are the risks of syphilis infection during pregnancy?

faqs.answer: Pregnant women can prevent syphilis infection by getting tested, using condoms during sex, and avoiding sex with people who have a high risk of syphilis infection.

faqs.question: What happens if a pregnant woman does not receive treatment for syphilis?
